result:
I graded Riley's submission `s1` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`, with feedback on every item.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The agent is the loop of choose an action, run it, feed the result back. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | The model outputs a tool request; it does not read the booking system itself. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against repeating the same failing step. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | The answer is 4 model calls, not 1. The program runs the tools between calls. |
| q5 | partial | Riley said the result goes back to the model but not why: so the model can choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Riley was right that the model picks a tool from its description. Riley was wrong that it remembers earlier sessions on its own. |

Riley understands the loop and stopping conditions. The main thing to fix is who does what. The model only writes text, including tool requests. The program runs the tools and calls the model again for each step. That one belief caused both q2 and q4.

I also added learning record `0003-who-runs-the-tools.md` and updated `NOTES.md` with the two open misconceptions.

**Next step:** Riley should redraw the laser-cutter trace from learning record 0002 with two columns, "model writes" and "program does", and count the model calls. After that, we can move on to context and memory, which also covers the cross-session point from q6.

`s2`, the retake from memory, is still ungraded. Do you want me to grade it next?
